subject: Observability packaging: tiered matrix, trial-credit path, and timeline
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acme-data.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@acme-data.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Observability retention tiers + trial credits (Acme)

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week — the dashboards look promising. Procurement asked me to get a clear matrix for observability add-ons (retention, tracing, advanced dashboards) so we can compare against our existing vendor. Two asks from Acme: 1) a concise price vs retention tier table (30/90/365/730 days) with seat vs usage options for dashboards, and 2) what trial/credit options you can offer to land a pilot covering our first 60 days.

I attached a quick spec of our expected monthly ingest volumes (request_spec.xlsx). High-level constraints:
- We need daily rollups and CSV export from the advanced dashboards.
- Tracing: retention of raw spans for 90 days minimum; long-term aggregation acceptable beyond that.
- Procurement prefers a single-line item on the invoice for add-ons if possible.

Can you send a couple of packaging options and a sample invoice for review? We aim to scope a 3-month pilot beginning mid-July.

Best,
Elena Soto
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Data

---
Attachments: request_spec.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acme-data.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability retention tiers + trial credits (Acme)

Elena,

Appreciate the spec — very helpful. See below for two packaging sketches and a pilot credit proposal. I attached a compact pricing sheet and a mock invoice so your procurement team can see line-item formatting (retention_pricing_sheet.xlsx, mock_invoice_ACME-2027.xlsx).

Option A — Slab (simpler for procurement)
- 30d retention: $X/month (base)
- 90d retention: base + incremental $/GB/month
- 365d, 730d: further tier multipliers
- Dashboards: seat-based license per editor; viewer tier free
- Tracing: retained raw spans for 90d included in 90d tier; archival priced per GB

Option B — Hybrid metered + seat
- Base observability bundle (includes ingestion + 30d retention) priced per monthly ingestion TB
- Overages billed per-GB for retention beyond the included tier
- Dashboards: seat license for editors + metered dashboard queries for heavy exports

Pilot credit proposal
- $15,000 observability credit, usable toward add-ons in first 60 days of pilot
- If you commit to a 12-month add-on contract post-pilot, we can apply a 20% discount to the add-on line for the first year (30% for 24-month commit)

Next steps
- If either option looks close, Karthik can run a quick modeling exercise against your request_spec to produce a sample invoice that matches procurement formatting.
- We can also waive the standard onboarding fee for add-ons if the contract is signed by July 15.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call with procurement tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Strategic Accounts — Observability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Observability retention tiers + trial credits (Acme)

Neha — thanks, that helps. A few clarifying questions from procurement and infra:
1) For Option A, can you make the add-on a single invoice line (Redwood can break down internally), and include an SKUnumber we can reference in our PO?
2) For Option B, how do you cap dashboard query overages? Procurement wants predictability — is there a monthly spend cap we can apply?
3) Regarding the pilot credit, will the $15k cover trace storage for 90 days at our projected ingest? If not, what delta should we expect on the first invoice?

Also copying a short legal question: do you support signature via DocuSign and can you accept our standard Master Services Agreement (I attached our procurement template to this thread in a separate email).

Elena

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Observability retention tiers + trial credits (Acme)

Forwarding with recommended structure + engineering notes. Quoted below for context.

Suggested commercial structure (compact, aligns with procurement ask):
- Single add-on invoice line: "Observability Add-ons (Retention + Tracing + Dashboards)" with SKU RD-OBS-ADD-01. Redwood maintains internal breakdown for finance.
- Tiering: list price follows slab table (30/90/365/730). Billing occurs monthly on actual ingest with a "committed slab" applied as a discounting anchor.
- Dashboard pricing: seat-based editors (monthly), viewers free. Exports (CSV) included up to N exports/month; beyond that, metered $/export or per-GB query cost.
- Overages & caps: we can offer a soft cap (notifications at 80/90%) and a hard cap opt-in for procurement that prevents bill above X% over committed spend.

Discount & pilot credits
- Pilot credit: $15k observability credit, applicable to add-on charges in first 60 days.
- Commit discounts: 20% for 12mo, 30% for 24mo (applies to add-on line only).
- One-time concessions: waive onboarding fee if signed by July 15 (Neha to confirm).

Engineering/ops notes (for Priyom / Kimberly):
- For 365/730 retention tiers we need to scope archival egress and query latency expectations in the SOW (attached draft sow_observability_draft.pdf).
- Tracing: raw-span retention >90d requires archival store; estimate additional $/GB month for retained raw spans beyond 90d.
- Dashboard exports: ensuring CSV export throughput for large rollups may require precomputed rollups (additional engineering time).

Delivery timeline (high level)
- Pilot kick: Mid-July
- Pilot sizing & sample invoice: 48-72 hours after we get final ingest numbers (Karthik to run model)
- SOW & PO: expected 2 weeks to finalize if legal redlines are minor

I can prepare the SKU'd invoice if Neha gives the green light; also recommend a short Pilot MPA to lock the credit and expected usage patterns.

-Karthik
